Index: workspace/fetch.sh
===================================================================
--- workspace/fetch.sh	
+++ workspace/fetch.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+set -e
+
+API="https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/accelerators_accelerateurs-aws"
+
+fetch() {
+    local url="$1"
+    local outfile="$2"
+    local status
+    status=$(curl -s -L -o "$outfile" -w "%{http_code}" "$url")
+    if [ "$status" -ge 400 ]; then
+        echo "Retrying $url after 5s..."
+        sleep 5
+        status=$(curl -s -L -o "$outfile" -w "%{http_code}" "$url")
+    fi
+    echo "$status" > "${outfile}.status"
+}
+
+fetch "$API" /workspace/repo.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/" /workspace/root_contents.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/CONTRIBUTING.md" /workspace/contributing.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/workflows" /workspace/workflows.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/dependabot.yml" /workspace/dependabot_yml.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.github/dependabot.yaml" /workspace/dependabot_yaml.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/renovate.json" /workspace/renovate.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/contents/.renovaterc.json" /workspace/renovaterc.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/commits" /workspace/commits.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/issues?state=open" /workspace/issues.json
+sleep 1
+fetch "$API/actions/runs" /workspace/actions_runs.json

If it exists but is just a placeholder or links without real instructions, write `Incomplete`. Allowed: `Present`/`Incomplete`/`Missing`/`Unknown`.
- `issue_response_quality`: Look at the 5 most recently updated open issues (API `issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc`, filter out PRs). For each, check if anyone other than the original reporter commented within the last 6 months (from 2026-07-13). If at least one issue has such a comment, write `Active`. If none, write `Stale`. Allowed: `Detailed`/`Version-only`/`No Releases`/`Unknown`.

- If you cannot determine a value, write exactly `Unknown`.
- Never derive a column from another `Unknown` column.

Alternatively, we can fetch everything via bash with curl and parse with jq. That might be easier.

Let's plan:

1. Fetch repo main page HTML to see README content and branch. But maybe raw README is easier.
2. Fetch raw README: `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/aia-eia/main/README.md`. If 404, try master.
3. Fetch SECURITY.md via raw URLs.
4. Fetch issues via API: `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/aia-eia/issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc | jq ...`. Sleep 1 after.
5. Fetch releases via API: `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/aia-eia/releases | jq ...`. Sleep 1 after.

But we need to be careful about API rate limits. The repo is public, so unauthenticated API requests have a limit of 60 per hour. We will make maybe 2 API calls. That's fine.

We need to parse the JSON. We can use bash with jq.

Let's start with a bash command to get the default branch and README. Actually, we can use `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/aia-eia` to get repo info including default branch. But that's an API call. Alternatively, we can just try `main` and `master` for raw README.

Let's do:

`curl -s -o /tmp/readme.md -w "%{http_code}" https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/aia-eia/main/README.md`

If 404, try master.

Also, we can fetch the HTML page of the repo to see the README rendered. That might give us a better view of bilingual content. But raw markdown is fine for reading text.

Let's do all of this in a bash script. We'll use `bash` tool.

We can write a script to:

- Try to fetch README.
- Try to fetch SECURITY.md in three locations.
- Fetch issues.
- Fetch releases.
- Sleep 1 between API calls.

Then we can read the files and analyze.

Let's do that.

set -e
# Try to fetch README
BRANCH="main"
HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /tmp/readme.md -w "%{http_code}" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/aia-eia/${BRANCH}/README.md")
if [ "$HTTP_CODE" != "200" ]; then
  BRANCH="master"
  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /tmp/readme.md -w "%{http_code}" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/aia-eia/${BRANCH}/README.md")
fi
echo "README branch: ${BRANCH}, HTTP: ${HTTP_CODE}"

# Fetch SECURITY.md in three locations
for path in "SECURITY.md" ".github/SECURITY.md" "docs/SECURITY.md"; do
  HTTP=$(curl -s -o "/tmp/sec_${path//\//_}" -w "%{http_code}" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/canada-ca/aia-eia/${BRANCH}/${path}")
  echo "SECURITY.md at ${path}: HTTP ${HTTP}"
done

# Fetch issues via API
curl -s -o /tmp/issues.json "https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/aia-eia/issues?state=open&sort=updated&direction=desc"
echo "Issues fetched"
sleep 1

# Fetch releases via API
curl -s -o /tmp/releases.json "https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/aia-eia/releases"
echo "Releases fetched"

# Save branch info
echo "$BRANCH" > /tmp/branch.txt

Algorithmic Impact Assessment
This project will host the next iteration of the Algorithmic Impact Assessment (AIA). It will consist in two main capabilities:

Offer a web-based questionnaire for end-users to assess their automated decision-making system
Offer a simple interface for the administrative team to update the questionnaire's questions, answers and scoring mechanism

The AIA is a critical piece of the Directive on Automated Decision-Making and we want to ensure its development is done in the open.
The users of this project will be Government of Canada employees assessing the impact of using an automated decision system, including Artificial Intelligence, as part of their programs and services.
As this assessment tool is open source, other countries and individiuals may wish to also leverage it and even contribute back to it.

Offrir une interface simple permettant à l'équipe administrative de mettre à jour les questions, les réponses et le mécanisme de notation du questionnaire.

L'EAI est un élément essentiel de la Directive sur la prise de décision automatisée et nous voulons nous assurer que son élaboration se fasse au grand jour.

We have all necessary data now. Let me analyze each field:

- bilingual: The repo page text clearly shows both English and French sections (Algorithmic Impact Assessment and Évaluation de l'incidence algorithmique). French section headers, French text, and French license text are present. So `Yes`.
- readme_clarity: The README content explains what the project is (Algorithmic Impact Assessment web-based questionnaire), who it's for (Government of Canada employees assessing automated decision systems), and how to use it (Getting Started / See the Wiki). It also describes how to contribute and license. So `Good`.
- security_policy: We found `SECURITY.md` in root. It contains responsible disclosure instructions (report by email to a specific person, in both English and French). This is real contact info, not a placeholder. So `Present`.
- issue_response_quality: The issues page shows 6 open issues, but all are from March 2019 and the repo was archived April 26, 2019 (read-only). Since there are no comments within the last 6 months (from July 2026, 6 months back is Jan 2026), and the repo is archived with no activity, none of the open issues have a recent comment from someone other than the reporter. So `Stale`.
- release_notes_quality: Releases page shows "There aren’t any releases here". So `No Releases`.

- **readme_clarity**: `Good` — The README clearly explains what the project is (a web-based questionnaire for assessing automated decision-making systems), who it is for (Government of Canada employees and potentially others), and how to get started (links to the Wiki and CONTRIBUTING.md).
